messages:
jessica-support: Hey team — Acme reported a billing gap: their invoice shows ~40% fewer embedding units charged than the dashboard. They used our bulk CSV embeddings + rerank last week. Can someone triage? :thinking:

mike-accounts: Noted. Do we have the invoice id and sample rows? Need invoice id to cross-ref ledger.

jessica-support: Invoice INV-2026-01-89, sent to acme@example.com. Customer pasted sample CSV with ~12k rows; each row is a text blob. They claim the model param was `model=embed-large-1536`.

luis-solutions: Quick question — did they use pairwise rerank mode or per-input embeddings then rerank? Pairwise rerank doubles embedding ops in some billing paths.

jessica-support: They said they called `/v1/embeddings` in batch (CSV upload) then a separate rerank request using the per-query set. Not pairwise from what they described.

danielle-engineer: I'll pull the serving logs. Can you share sample request IDs or the CSV header? If they uploaded via UI, I need the manifest id. Also flagging prod-oncall for routing/variant fallback suspicion.

jessica-support: They gave a sample request id: req_0a9f3b. CSV header: `id,text` and they included `model=embed-large-1536` in the request metadata.

prod-oncall: Pulling logs now: `logsearch --q "req_0a9f3b" --svc embeddings --from 2026-01-10 --to 2026-01-11`. I see the request landed in region-us-east and the scheduler routed to node pool gpustack-02. There's a routing note: "fallback: embed-lite-1024" for that run due to transient capacity shortage.

sam-billing-bot: Ledger note found for req_0a9f3b: billed_embedding_units: 1024 per vector for that batch. Invoice aggregated totals match ledger (so invoice isn't wrong), but dashboard was showing model profile 1536 dims for the customer when they viewed recent runs (cached model profile).

danielle-engineer: That explains mismatch between invoice (actual billed dims) and customer's dashboard expectation (profile alias 1536). Why did we fallback to 1024? Check routing policy: if dedicated capacity for 1536 wasn't available, scheduler will route to compatible variant (embed-lite-1024) to maintain availability. Billing currently charges actual dims used (1024).

luis-solutions: Customer says they didn't opt into downgrade. We need to surface fallback info to customers and include a note in invoices if a fallback variant was used. Also need to consider automatic retroactive credit or fix for cases where quality regression is material.

mike-accounts: For this account (enterprise with committed spend), we can offer a one-off credit while we sort policies. Let's prepare an audit and recommend next steps.

danielle-engineer: Repro steps for internal audit: 1) download batch payload (we have the manifest). 2) replay locally with `--force-variant=embed-lite-1024` and `--force-variant=embed-large-1536` to confirm dim outputs and metrics. 3) check scheduler trace for that window `2026-01-10T02:00Z` -> `2026-01-10T04:00Z`. I'll attach diffs.

jessica-support: I've told Acme we're investigating and will follow up with a timeline. They've escalated to their procurement team asking for an invoice explanation.

prod-oncall: Adding notes: routing fallback we saw is working as designed but opaque. Action items: (A) surface fallback variant in request logs + dashboard for last-run metadata, (B) add invoice line or note when fallback reduces billed dims relative to requested model, (C) add a reconciliation tool for customers to compare requested-model-profile vs billed-variant-profile.

sam-billing-bot: Creating ticket BILL-6219 to capture invoice annotation + retro-bill/credit options.

mike-accounts: I'll draft a credit proposal: refund difference between 1536 and 1024 unit price for affected rows or a fixed goodwill credit. Need count of affected vectors from audit.

danielle-engineer: Quick heads-up — there is an edge-case where mixed-batch uploads (some rows flagged with `model=embed-large-1536` and some unspecified) can cause the scheduler to pick one variant and apply it to whole batch, resulting in uniform billed dims that differ from per-row requested model. Recommend rejecting mixed-model batches or enforcing per-row model compatibility.

luis-solutions: Good call. For now, tell Acme the root cause is scheduler fallback + mixed-batch behavior. Apologize, offer credit, and give timeline (ETA 48h for audit, 7d for billing adjustment).

jessica-support: Copying that to the customer thread. Acme asked whether we'll retro-bill to 1536 to match what they expected — we should confirm legal/finance before promising.

mike-accounts: Confirmed: don't promise retro-billing. Offer credit while product addresses UX and billing transparency. We'll prepare a statement.

danielle-engineer: I'm attaching the minimal repro commands for future incident notes:

```bash
# replay with 1024 variant
redwood replay --manifest s3://manifests/acme-jan10.csv --model embed-lite-1024 --out audit/1024.json

# replay with 1536 variant
redwood replay --manifest s3://manifests/acme-jan10.csv --model embed-large-1536 --out audit/1536.json

# compare dims
jq '.vectors[].dim' audit/1536.json | sort | uniq -c
```

jessica-support: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with Acme after audit results. :thumbsup:

prod-oncall: Filing follow-up: visibility change + scheduler policy review. Tagging eng-routing and billing teams.

mike-accounts: Putting provisional credit on hold until audit confirms affected vector count.

luis-solutions: I'll draft customer-facing language to explain fallback behavior and next steps.

jessica-support: Closing loop for now — will post audit summary back here when available.
